evaluation_dataset: Clinical (60 images, Almaty medical centre, Topcon-class camera)
cross_validation: 5-fold patient-level stratified on IDRiD, Clinical held out as test
notes: Read the PAIRED confidence intervals. At n = 60 the per-arm unpaired bootstrap intervals overlap (C [0.4511, 0.6007], D [0.5338, 0.6742]); significance comes from the paired test, where both arms are scored on the very same 60 images.

The pipeline is ahead on the internal IDRiD CV in 4 of the 5 folds (margins +0.1262, +0.0952, +0.0906, +0.0287), with one marginal inversion of -0.0057 on baseline's strongest fold — well inside the between-fold std (0.031-0.038). Report it as 'four of five folds, one marginal inversion' rather than naming a fold: which fold inverts is not stable.
The clinical gain here (+7.98pp) is comparable to the full-EyePACS gain (+6.55pp), so the pipeline advantage is NOT specific to the small-data regime and does not wash out as data grows.
Absolute F1 of 0.51-0.59 is expected for training on 516 images and testing in a different clinic; the informative quantity is the difference between arms.
The +/- values are the spread across the 5 training folds, not per-instance uncertainty on the hold-out.
